# Setting up the lab

A rooted Android x86_64 emulator running frida-server, plus the demo app
minapp. The native chapters use a small C program built later.

## 1. Boot the emulator

Create an AVD with the Android command-line tools (API 34, x86_64, Google
APIs is a known-good combination). Then:

```bash
$ export ANDROID_HOME=$HOME/android-sdk
$ export PATH=$ANDROID_HOME/emulator:$ANDROID_HOME/platform-tools:$PATH
$ emulator -avd <avd-name> -writable-system -no-snapshot -no-audio -no-boot-anim &
$ adb wait-for-device
$ adb root
```

`adb root` restarts adbd as root on the emulator. Check:

```bash
$ adb shell id
uid=0(root) ...
```

![Emulator](img/first_steps/emulator-home.png)

> **Note:** Linux Yama restricts ptrace attachments by default. A native
> process started in another terminal is not a descendant of the rizin
> process, so local attachment fails with `Unable to access /proc/<pid>/mem:
> Permission denied` while `kernel.yama.ptrace_scope` is `1`. Set it to 0
> once after each host boot, then verify the value:

```bash
$ cat /proc/sys/kernel/yama/ptrace_scope
1
$ sudo sysctl -w kernel.yama.ptrace_scope=0
kernel.yama.ptrace_scope = 0
$ cat /proc/sys/kernel/yama/ptrace_scope
0
```

## 2. Install and run frida-server

Download `frida-server` for `android-x86_64` from the Frida releases page,
matching the plugin's frida-core version. Decompress it, then:

```bash
$ adb push frida-server /data/local/tmp/frida-server
$ adb shell 'chmod 755 /data/local/tmp/frida-server'
$ adb shell '/data/local/tmp/frida-server -D &'
$ adb shell 'ps -A | grep frida'
root       2051  1    12723072 147564 do_sys_poll   0 S frida-server
```

![frida-server running](img/first_steps/frida-server-ps.png)

Verify the host sees the device and its processes:

```bash
$ frida-ps -U
 PID  Name
----  ------------------------------------------------------
 854  SIM Toolkit
 859  Settings
 2100 FridaMin
 ...
```

![frida-ps over USB](img/first_steps/frida-ps-usb.png)

`-U` selects the USB device. `FridaMin` is the demo app label, which is
also the process name we attach to.

> **Note:** this emulator's `su` is not a full toybox `su`: do not write
> `adb shell su -c '...'`. `adb root` is already root, so run frida-server
> directly.

## 3. Install the demo app

Download the prebuilt emulator APK (x86_64) from
<https://t.me/rzfrida/25>. Package `re.frida.minapp`, label `FridaMin`.
A physical non-rooted phone needs the gadget APK instead. See
[Non-rooted devices](../remote_access/non_rooted_gadget.qmd).

Uninstall first if a differently signed copy is already present:

```bash
$ adb uninstall re.frida.minapp
$ adb install -r minapp.apk
$ adb shell am start -n re.frida.minapp/.MainActivity
```

The app opens with a status line, a license key field and five buttons:
Activate License, Upgrade to Premium, Earn Coins, Load Plugin and
Run Tests, plus a feedback line under them.

![minapp UI](img/first_steps/minapp-ui.png)

Confirm the native side registered everything:

```bash
$ adb logcat -d | grep rz-native
... JNI_OnLoad -- registering native methods via RegisterNatives
... registered 1 method on SecretVault
... JNI_OnLoad complete -- 8 methods registered across 4 classes
```

The native Linux demo used later is built in
[Building the target](../native_journey/building_the_target.qmd).

## 4. One-command verification

The plugin talks to the emulator through USB, so no forward is needed:

```bash
$ rizin -N -q -c 'fridaoj frida://attach/usb//FridaMin' malloc://512
{"ok":true,"result":{"action":"attach","pid":2100,"resumed":false,"state":"attached"}}
```

If this works, the lab is up.
